To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the petunia PhCCD7 mutant is involved in the production of both a negative and a positive branch branching signal and that the branching phenotype of this plant is more severe than that of the PhCCDC8 mutant.
in petunias, the CCD7 gene is involved in the production of both negative and positive branch branching signals.
in Petunia hybride, the carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase (CCD7) gene is involved in both the production of a negative branching signal and a positive branching signal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of branching in petunia and shows that the loss of CCD7 or CCD7 and CCD6 is sufficient to produce a mutant phenotype.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PhCCD genes are involved in both positive and negative feedback control of branching.

in petunias, CCD7 and/or CCD8 are required for the synthesis of a negative branch signal, which is produced in the roots and transported to the aerial portion of the plant, and that the loss of CCD7 and/or 8 results in the loss of this signal, leading to the increased production of a positive branch signal, which results in the increased number of branches produced.
PhCCD7 and PhCCD8 have both positive and negative effects on petunia branching.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PhCCD8 gene is involved in the synthesis of a branch-suppressive compound, whereas the PhCCD6 and PhCCD7 genes are involved in the synthesis and/or regulation of a branch-promoting compound.
in petunias, the loss of a branch-suppressive signal results in the production of a new, more potent branch-promoting signal.
the CCD genes in petunia function as both positive and negative regulators of plant architecture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of CCD7 and CCD 8 in petunias is not as simple as in Arabidopsis, where they are both involved only in the production of a branching inhibitor.
the regulation of branching is complex, and the same gene may act as both a positive and negative regulator of branching depending on the species in which it is expressed.
the role of the CCD7 gene in petunia differs from its role in Arabidopsis.
